keyPoints.text: onHand counts units physically recorded at a warehouse; reserved counts units promised to orders but not shipped.
keyPoints.quote: `reserved` means units already promised to orders but not shipped

keyPoints.text: Available-to-promise is on-hand minus reserved, clamped at zero.
It is a domain rule because it decides whether an order can move from pending to allocated.

questions.prompt: Explain why reservation demand must be grouped by SKU, what counts as a valid quantity, and how planning differs from applying.

keyPoints.text: Two lines for the same SKU (14 and 9) each fit under 22 but together ask for 23.
keyPoints.quote: Each line is less than 22, but the order asks for 23 total.

keyPoints.text: Checking lines independently treats one shared stock pool as two separate pools.
keyPoints.quote: Checking lines independently treats one shared stock pool as two separate pools.

keyPoints.text: Grouping by SKU is safe only because the caller passes balances for one warehouse.
keyPoints.quote: Grouping by SKU alone is safe only because the caller passes balances for one warehouse

keyPoints.text: A valid quantity is a positive safe integer; zero, negatives, fractions, NaN and infinity are rejected.
planReservation reports invalid lines in its normal decision shape.

keyPoints.text: applyReservation throws because it is a state transformation that cannot return a meaningful balance after an invalid mutation.

keyPoints.text: The grouping is the requestedBySku map in the planner.

questions.prompt: Explain what the service's two checks and its transaction do and do not guarantee for concurrent reservations.

keyPoints.text: planReservation produces the decision the API reports back.
keyPoints.quote: `planReservation` produces the decision the API reports back.

keyPoints.text: Inside the write loop applyReservation re-checks each per-SKU total, and a throw rolls the whole transaction back.
keyPoints.quote: if it throws, the whole transaction rolls back

keyPoints.text: The write loop also aggregates by SKU, so two lines for one SKU produce one increment and one reservation row.
keyPoints.quote: produces one `InventoryItem` increment and one `StockReservation` row

keyPoints.text: The transaction makes the multi-record workflow of stock, status, event, outbox and audit atomic.
keyPoints.quote: the transaction makes the multi-record workflow atomic

keyPoints.text: Both checks compare against balances read at the start of the transaction, and the increment is unconditional.
keyPoints.quote: both checks compare against the `balances` read at the start of the transaction

keyPoints.text: Whether two concurrent reservations can both pass depends on database isolation, not on this code.
keyPoints.quote: depends on the database's isolation, not on this code
